result:
I wrote 18 pre-UI cases for the registration ticket. The kit checker passes on the Markdown file with 0 problems. It can't read the CSV, so the CSV is unchecked.

**Files**
- `qa/cases/registration-spec.md` (the checked file)
- `qa/cases/registration-spec.csv`

**CSV:** The checker only accepts the Markdown layout, so it reported "No cases found" for the CSV. The CSV holds the same cases, one row per step, in the layout from `cases.csv.md`.

**Header and sources:** The header says `Atlas: none yet`. There is no atlas, so I skipped the grounding check. The checker confirmed that every ‹expected: …› text carries a source back to a ticket criterion (`ticket:tickets/registration-spec.md#AC<n>`). It counted 26 such texts in the Markdown file.

**Knowledge base:** There is no `qa/kb`, so no decisions or known issues were applied and nothing was answered from the knowledge base.

**Mismatches:** There is no app to compare against, so section 1 lists 12 questions about gaps in the ticket instead. The main ones:
- The login-page link that opens the registration form has no text in the ticket.
- Nothing says what happens with a password longer than 40 characters, so I wrote no case for it.
- Nothing says what happens when the terms box isn't ticked, whether the button is disabled or an error appears. TC-REG-014 only checks that no account is created.
- The ticket doesn't say what the Google sign-up does. TC-REG-018 only checks that the button is shown.
- Which security questions are offered, and where "This cannot be changed later!" appears, are also open.
- Email uniqueness: it isn't stated whether the check ignores case.
- Message punctuation is inconsistent in the ticket: two messages have no full stop.

**Next steps**
- Once the screen is built, run `/reconqa:reconcile qa/cases/registration-spec.md`. Only reconcile turns the ‹expected› texts into real screen text.
- When the team has answered the questions, record the answers with `/reconqa:kb answer`.
- Nothing was sent
